# PlasmidPop

> PlasmidPop is a free, browser-based DNA sequence editor and plasmid viewer, comparable in scope to SnapGene. It runs entirely in the browser: no account, no upload, no server round-trip, and it works offline once loaded. MIT licensed.

There is no backend. Documents are stored in the browser (IndexedDB); a document leaves the app only as a download or as a share link that carries it in the URL fragment. The only third-party host is NCBI, contacted only for the accessions or gene names the user types (and a primer pair goes to Primer-BLAST only in a link the user opens). Optional self-hosted Matomo page-view statistics never include sequence content or file names and can be switched off in Help.

## What it does

- Formats: GenBank (.gb, .gbk, .ape), FASTA, SnapGene .dna/.rna/.prot (read and write), GenPept and protein FASTA, AB1 traces, FASTQ (gzipped or not), ZIP of sequence files, records from NCBI by accession.
- Viewing: linear sequence view and zoomable circular map (Canvas), features, translations, GC content; export as SVG, PNG or PDF.
- Editing: typing, copy and paste with features, reverse complement, set origin, circular/linear, undo/redo with a history that survives reload; feature editor with GenBank locations (join, complement, origin-spanning); detect common features.
- Analysis: restriction sites (about 130 bundled enzymes, or REBASE imported by the user), gels, diagnostic digests, ORFs, six-frame translation, primer design and checking, pairwise and multiple sequence alignment, protein properties, CRISPR guide design (SpCas9, SaCas9, Cas12a, custom PAM; off-targets only within open documents).
- Sequencing: Sanger reads aligned to an expected construct or assembled into a contig; clone verification.
- Simulated cloning (the Bench): digest, ligation, Golden Gate, Gibson, In-Fusion/NEBuilder, Gateway, overlap-extension PCR, MoClo/Yeast Toolkit plans, PCR, site-directed mutagenesis.

## What it does not do

- No accounts, sync, team libraries or real-time collaboration; no server-side computation.
- It never writes to the user's disk except as a download; the file you opened is not modified.
- Not aimed at genomes: sequences above about 10 Mb are out of scope.
- Primer thermodynamics are a compact nearest-neighbour model checked against Primer3, not a reimplementation of its thal; melting temperatures are good to about 2 C at 500 nM oligo and 50 mM monovalent salt.
- Sanger repeat placement weighs the chosen place and at most eight alternatives; reads fitting only beyond that keep their best place with a warning. Sanger assembly has no real-world benchmark against another assembler yet.
- Correctness is checked against independent oracles (e.g. Primer3, Biopython) and mutation testing, which is run by hand before each release, not in CI.
